### Given Data:
* Front view (FV) length $= 55\text{ mm}$
* Inclination of line to V.P. ($	heta$) $= 30^ceil$
* Position: Parallel to and $30\text{ mm}$ above H.P., one end $20\text{ mm}$ in front of V.P.

### Step-by-Step Construction Procedure:
1. **Reference Line and Basic Positions:**
   * Draw a reference line $XY$.
   * Since the line is parallel to H.P. and $30\text{ mm}$ above it, the front view will be a horizontal line parallel to $XY$ at a distance of $30\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.
   * One end ($A$) is $20\text{ mm}$ in front of V.P., so its top view $a$ lies on a projector $20\text{ mm}$ below $XY$.

2. **Front View Projection:**
   * Mark front view end $a'$ at distance $30\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.
   * Draw the front view line $a'b'$ of length $55\text{ mm}$ parallel to $XY$ (since the line is parallel to H.P., its front view shows true length if it were parallel, but wait—let's check inclinations).
   * *Correction/Refinement:* The problem states the *front view* is $55\text{ mm}$ long and inclined at $30^	ext{o}$ to V.P? No, the *line* is inclined at $30^	ext{o}$ to V.P. When a line is parallel to H.P., its front view length is equal to its plan length (top view length), and inclination of front view with $XY$ is zero.

3. **Finding True Length (TL):**
   * Since the line is parallel to H.P., the Top View (TV) gives the True Length (TL) and true inclination with V.P. ($	heta = 30^	ext{o}$). 
   * Length of FV $= L \cos(	ext{angle with HP})$, but here HP angle is $0^	ext{o}$, so FV length = True Length $	imes 	ext{something}$? Wait, if a line is parallel to H.P., its Front view length is equal to True Length $\times \cos(\text{angle with HP})$? No, Front view is projected on V.P. If line is inclined to V.P. at $30^	ext{o}$ and parallel to H.P., then:
     * $\text{Top View Length} = \text{True Length} \times \cos(30^	ext{o})$.
     * $\text{Front View Length} = \text{True Length}$ (projected directly as parallel to $XY$).
   * Therefore, True Length = Length of Front View $= 55\text{ mm}$.

4. **Final Projections:**
   * Front view $a'b'$ is a horizontal line of $55\text{ mm}$ length drawn $30\text{ mm}$ above $XY$.
   * Top view $ab$ is inclined at $30^	ext{o}$ to $XY$ starting from projector of $a$, with length equal to $55 \times \cos(30^	ext{o}) = 47.63\text{ mm}$.
proTip: Remember that when a line is parallel to one plane (here H.P.), its projection on that plane (here FV) shows the true length of the line.
